_**Agent (gpt-6-astra 2026-09-22 05:02:01Z)**_

你提的方式可行：共用一份 Mermaid，再交給現成 renderer 輸出，無須自行寫 ASCII 排版。

- [`mermaid-ascii`](https://github.com/AlexanderGrooff/mermaid-ascii) 有可直接引用的 Go rendering API，適合內建到 lazyclash，讓 CLI／TUI 不必另裝終端 renderer。
- [`termaid`](https://github.com/fasouto/termaid) 也能在終端顯示 Mermaid，但需要 Python 環境。
- [`mermaid-cli`](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli) 的 `mmdc` 可輸出 SVG，適合作為選用的匯出工具。

另外，現在**已有 `--target <Tab>` 補全**，候選來自本機註冊的 targets，不會連 SSH。Zsh 載入 completion 後就能用；設定方式已有 `lazyclash completion install zsh`。Wizard 仍值得保留，因為能同時搜尋、看名稱和多選。

I’m thinking about whether ASCII can handle a max node label of 80 cells. If the graph's full name goes long, it could reach 4096 characters, especially with 150 nodes times 4000. I need to check if the max for total cells is indeed 8000, and that label lengths are limited to 48 cells in terminals. Also, can Mermaid export handle this without truncating? The common graph-to-Mermaid conversion needs careful observation on label lengths too.**Evaluating Mermaid cycles**

I’m considering that full Mermaid always emits cycles. If ASCII detects these cycles, it shouldn’t call the renderer and should return an error about "cyclic dependency; use relations or Mermaid." It's a safe approach, but cycles can still be displayed in diagnostics with a fallback. I think the plan could show these cycles if they cause failure. I’m thinking about the runtime map and whether it needs the provider object credentials for new nodes with known fields. It seems I can just map raw data to JSON arrays at runtime.
